item: Feed fetch state is read as the columns each call site uses (tag coverage, the due filter, the language-equilibrium block), not as entities
summary: The three sites loaded every FeedFetchState row as an entity to read two to four columns (etag and last_modified included). Measured on the seeded stores, same statement before and after: tag_coverage (86,000 states) 1,216-1,312 ms and 152.5 MB to 548-571 ms and 47.9 MB; _filter_due_feeds (57,333 feed ids) 943-991 ms and 111.3 MB to 321-352 ms and 27.2 MB. SIDE EFFECTS PROVEN, none lost: the entity load only filled the pass-level session's identity map (workers open their own session_scope sessions), FeedFetchState has no relationship and no mapper-level load listener (mapper listeners are on Source and Article insert/update), and the session-level hooks (do_orm_execute, before_flush, after_begin) fire equally for column queries. feed_is_due accepts FeedFetchState | Row | None and reads attributes by name. Q's pin tests re-run whole: test_gates_survive_an_interrupt, test_worker_only_callers_pinned, test_get_routes_side_effects. tests/test_feed_state_projection.py (2 tests, both fail on main). test_every_started_thread_and_written_file_is_accounted_for fails identically on unchanged main in a duckdb-installed environment, because bulletin GETs start the rollup-build thread and write rollup_build.json; this PR neither causes nor changes it.
